verdict.rationale: `bun install` is documented to install all `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, plus `peerDependencies` by default, from `package.json`. It covers workspaces in a monorepo, and `--frozen-lockfile` installs the exact locked versions for a reproducible bootstrap. Dependency lifecycle scripts like `postinstall` do not run unless the package is listed in `trustedDependencies`, and community reports note occasional install crashes on Windows. Missing for 10: dependency lifecycle scripts running by default without `trustedDependencies` configuration, independent hands-on confirmation of clean fresh-clone bootstraps.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: Installs all `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, and `optionalDependencies`. Bun installs `peerDependencies` by default.
if your project has a `package.json`, you can use `bun install`.
For reproducible installs, use `--frozen-lockfile`. Bun installs the exact versions specified in the lockfile and does not update it.
